subject: I-O status
notes: kb/Work PB1512 landed (w67p). cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'A permanent error exists and no further information is available concerning the input-output operation' -> OK §9.1.13.6 1). Every statement that touches the host now maps a host IOException to an I-O status: OPEN/CLOSE/DELETE FILE (before), WRITE/WRITE ADVANCING/REWRITE ('34'/'30', kb/Work PB1192), and now READ and START FIRST/LAST (SequentialConnector.Read / StartFirstLast -> ReadFailed: '30', file position invalidated, §14.9.30.4 GR18 / §14.9.41.4 GR7). Keyed record verbs never touch the host between OPEN and CLOSE (the store is in memory). Sibling sweep: an unsuccessful OPEN's handle release (FileConnector.Open -> AbandonOpen, KeyedConnector.ReleaseFileLock) could throw outside OPEN's try - now caught, the OPEN's own status stands; OPEN … REVERSED counted the records AFTER the open returned, against SharedOpenAttempt's PB713 rule - now counted inside the OPEN body (ReversedRequested). Witness: a real host read failure per host (Linux /proc/self/mem EIO; Windows a locked byte range) -> '30', then '46', and START FIRST '30'. retired-witness: unit:FileBoundaryTests.SequentialRead_HostFailure_Is30_AndInvalidatesThePosition (renamed, not lost: the test pinned the pre-PB1541 '46' after a '30' READ; the permanent error now remains in effect (9.1.13.1), so it asserts '30' again and is named for that)
